# `endpoints/cors-wildcard-credentials`: CORS allows any origin together with credentials

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family    | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| endpoints | high             | 8.0                      | [CWE-942](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/942.html), [CWE-346](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/346.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

CORS configurations that let any website make credentialed requests:

- `cors({ origin: true, credentials: true })`, an origin callback that always allows, or
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` set from the request's `Origin` header together with
  `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` (Express, Fastify, Next.js handlers, manual
  headers): **high**.
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with credentials (browsers reject it, but it shows the
  intent and usually turns into reflection).
- `next.config` `headers()` entries, parsed statically.
- A permissive origin without credentials on code that relies on cookies for
  authentication: reported lower, because it is one config change away from exploitable.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

With Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, browsers send the user's cookies on cross-site requests. If the server also echoes back whatever Origin the request had (cors({ origin: true }), a callback that always allows, or res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', req.headers.origin)), any website the user visits can call your API as them and read the responses. A literal "*" with credentials is rejected by browsers, but it shows the intent, and the usual "fix" is reflection.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- CORS allows any origin on code that relies on cookies for authentication. Without credentials: true browsers will not send the cookies, so this is not directly exploitable, but it is one config change away. Restrict the origin list.
- CORS echoes any request origin and allows credentials: any website can make authenticated requests as your users and read the responses.
- CORS combines Access-Control-Allow-Origin "*" with credentials. Browsers reject this combination, so cross-origin calls fail. Use an explicit origin list, not reflection.

## How to fix

Allow an explicit list of trusted origins. Only set credentials: true when cookies must cross origins. Never echo the request Origin without checking it against the list.

### Vulnerable

```ts
app.use(cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }));
```

### Fixed

```ts
const allowedOrigins = ['https://app.example.com', 'https://admin.example.com'];
app.use(
  cors({
    origin: (origin, cb) => cb(null, !origin || allowedOrigins.includes(origin)),
    credentials: true,
  }),
);
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Public APIs** that use `origin: '*'` **without** credentials and without cookie auth are
  fine and not reported.
- **Origin allowlists** (an array, a regex, or a callback that checks a list) are not
  reported. An origin callback is reported only when it visibly allows every origin.
- **Limitations:** CORS set by a CDN, gateway or hosting configuration (`vercel.json`
  headers, nginx) is invisible.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line endpoints/cors-wildcard-credentials -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  endpoints/cors-wildcard-credentials: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-942](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/942.html): Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
- [CWE-346](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/346.html): Origin Validation Error
